title: shortcuts with pressed Alt don't work when keymap is changed
author: mozdzierz

status.label: Waiting for current-build and IME confirmation
status.detail: The report gives a Japanese IME/right-Alt sequence, but the July 28 request to retest on 0.100.2+ and test without IME is unanswered.

next_action: Await the existing current-version and no-IME comparison before selecting a fix path.

judgment.rationale: The report provides a specific sequence: Japanese IME, right-Alt shortcuts that send Polish characters, then a layout change while right Alt remains held; the second shortcut then emits the wrong character. The latest maintainer request asks whether this persists on 0.100.2 or newer and whether it is specific to the Polish Programmers layout. There is no author response.
evidence: The issue reports PowerToys 0.84.1 and maps right Alt+A to ą and right Alt+C to ć while using Microsoft Japanese IME.
After changing the keyboard layout to Polish (Programmers) or US International while keeping right Alt held, the reporter says the first shortcut produces ą but the next yields c instead of ć.
The September 2024 similar-issue suggestions #34193 and #22988 do not establish a covering fix; #22988 was closed as a duplicate of a different report.
The July 28, 2026 maintainer comment asks for a 0.100.2-or-newer retest and a comparison without IME; no later author response appears.
judgment.recommended_action: Wait for the requested supported-build and no-IME comparison; then reproduce the reported held-right-Alt layout-switch sequence against the current engine.
requested_evidence: Current PowerToys version and persistence on 0.100.2 or newer
Whether the same sequence reproduces without Japanese IME
Whether the failure depends on the Polish (Programmers) layout

fix_assessment.rationale: A code change is not supportable until the unanswered current-build and no-IME checks determine whether this held-Alt layout-switch behavior remains and which input path fails. This wait does not dismiss the historical report.

issue_context.summary: A right-Alt shortcut that emits Polish characters works until the keyboard layout changes while right Alt remains held; then a later shortcut emits the wrong character.
known_information: The issue is open and reports PowerToys 0.84.1 with Microsoft Japanese IME.
The reported mappings are right Alt+A to ą and right Alt+C to ć.
After changing layout to Polish (Programmers) or US International while holding right Alt, the reporter observed ąc instead of ąć.
A maintainer requested a 0.100.2-or-newer retest and a test without IME on July 28, 2026; no response followed.
inferences: The failure may depend on IME composition or on how the held right-Alt modifier is tracked across an input-layout change; neither mechanism is confirmed.
Issue #34193 also concerns Polish-layout behavior but describes a different symptom and does not establish a duplicate.
issue_context.analysis: The original reproduction is unusually specific and can guide a local test, but it is from PowerToys 0.84.1 and the latest maintainer questions remain unanswered. The response should not repeat a generic diagnostics request; first establish current impact and whether Japanese IME is required.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body and both comments, including the exact mappings and held-right-Alt layout-change sequence.
Checked suggested issue #34193; it concerns a separate Polish-layout/IME symptom and is not a confirmed duplicate.
Checked #22988; it was closed as a duplicate of #3641, not a fix for this reported sequence.
Confirmed the July 28, 2026 request remains unanswered.

information_gaps.information: Whether the held-right-Alt sequence still fails on PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer and whether it reproduces without Japanese IME.
information_gaps.why_needed: The report is from 0.84.1, and IME/layout interaction is the main unresolved distinction for choosing the owning code path.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Retest the exact mappings and layout-switch sequence on 0.100.2 or newer, then repeat without Japanese IME and report the active layout.
